22001.description: A vaulted passage of black stone runs beneath the castle's outer works, its roof lost in a darkness no torch has warmed in an age. To the north the floor drops away into a tangle of braced sticks, the old way toward the Lost Castle. An iron-bound door in the south wall gives onto the entrance chambers, while the pathway around the castle leads off east and west through low arches crusted with ash. The air is still and smells of cold iron.

14205.description: The pathway hugs the foot of the castle wall, a ledge of cracked flagstones scattered with bone splinters and windblown ash. Overhead the sky is a low lid of grey cloud that never seems to move. The vaulted passage toward the Lost Castle lies back to the west, and the path runs on east beneath a line of iron spikes driven into the stone. Every gust carries a faint taste of smoke.

14206.description: Here the wall bellies outward over the path, its black blocks scorched in long tongues as if great fires once licked up their face. A burned banner hangs from a rusted bracket, nothing left of it but a blackened rag that snaps in the wind. The flagstones are split and heaved, and the path picks its way between them east and west. Somewhere above, a loose shutter bangs without rhythm.

14207.description: A row of pikes stands along the outer edge of the path, each crowned with a weathered skull turned to face the castle. Beyond them the ground falls away into a grey haze where nothing grows. The wall here bears a deep crack wide enough to take an arm, and cold air breathes out of it. The path continues east and west along the stones.

14208.description: Ash lies ankle-deep on this stretch of the pathway, soft and grey and marked by nothing at all. The wind lifts it in slow curls that drift along the foot of the wall and settle again. Iron rings set into the stonework at shoulder height still hold the rusted ends of chains, their other ends long since gone. The way runs on east, and back west toward the castle's dark passage.

14209.description: A fallen buttress has spilled its blocks across half the path, leaving a narrow gap between rubble and wall to squeeze through. Shattered bones are mixed into the debris, old enough to have taken on the colour of the stone. Far off, beyond the haze, a bell tolls once and falls silent. The pathway runs east toward a turn in the wall and west along the castle's flank.

14210.description: The pathway reaches a corner of the castle, where two great walls meet in a tower of black stone that rises out of sight into the cloud. Arrow slits stare down from its face, dark and empty. The path bends here, running south along the next face of the wall and west back the way it came. The wind is fiercer at the corner, moaning through the slits like a voice.

14211.description: Along this face of the castle the wall is studded with iron spikes, each as long as a man's arm and red with rust. Scraps of cloth and leather cling to some of them, faded to the grey of everything else. The pathway runs north to the corner tower and south along the foot of the wall. Underfoot the stones are slick with a dark, oily grime that never dries.

14212.description: The pathway ends abruptly where a great slab of the wall has fallen outward and buried the way beneath a mound of broken stone. Nothing lies beyond the slab but grey haze and the endless wind. A charred standard pole juts from the rubble, its banner burned away to a few blackened threads. The only way on is north, back along the wall.

14102.description: The entrance chambers open into a broad room of black stone, its ceiling held up by squat pillars bound in iron bands. Heavy doors stand to the north, where the dark passage leads out toward the pathway and the Lost Castle. Halls run off east and west along the inner wall, and to the south a wide arch opens on the Inner Hall. Burned banners hang in tatters from the pillars, and the floor is scored by countless iron-shod feet.

rooms.14104: This hall runs straight along the inner face of the castle wall, low-roofed and narrow, its stones sweating a cold damp. Iron sconces line the wall at regular intervals, every one of them empty and furred with rust. Mold spreads in pale grey blooms along the seams of the floor. The hall continues east and west into gloom.
rooms.14105: The hall widens slightly around a stone bench set into the wall, its seat worn hollow by long-dead sentries. Above it someone has scratched a tally into the stone, hundreds of marks in rows until the last line breaks off unfinished. The smell of old ash hangs heavy in the air. Narrow passages lead on east and west.
rooms.14107: A spiral stair climbs out of the corner of this hall, its steps cracked and slick, rising up toward the ragged walkway atop the castle. A thin draught falls down the stairwell, carrying the moan of wind from the battlements. The hall itself turns here, running west along the wall and south into deeper shadow. Rusted chains hang from the ceiling at the foot of the stair, swaying a little in the draught.
rooms.14109: The hall runs straight and narrow, the inner wall on one side and a row of arrow-loops on the other, every shutter nailed fast. Bones have been swept into a heap against the foot of the wall, as though someone meant to clear them and never came back. The stone floor slopes gently as the hall runs south, and climbs north toward the stair.
rooms.14111: Water seeps down the wall here in thin black streaks, pooling in a shallow channel cut along the floor. The channel is choked with rust-red sludge and smells of iron and rot. A broken halberd is bolted to the wall as a trophy, its blade notched in some forgotten battle. The hall runs north and south, its far ends lost in the dark.
rooms.14112: A great iron grille is set into the ceiling of this stretch, and through it falls a faint grey light from somewhere far above. The light shows walls blackened by fire and a floor strewn with the brittle remains of shields, their devices long since burned away. The hall continues north, and south it narrows toward a darker stretch where the air turns stale and close.
rooms.22155: The floor of this black hall is not stone at all but a skin of rotten planks laid over a pit, and they groan beneath the slightest weight. From the depths below rises a stench of old death and the faint glint of upturned blades. Darkness swallows everything but the creak of failing timber. The way north and the way south both lie across the same treacherous boards.
rooms.14116: The hall turns along the wall here, and the stonework changes to great rough blocks stacked without mortar, each one larger than a cart. The gaps between them have been packed with bone, skulls and thighbones wedged tight to hold the courses level. The air is cold and utterly still. The way runs east toward a heap of charred masonry and west into deeper dark.
rooms.22025: A sickly, sweetish reek fills this dark stretch of hall, thick enough to taste. Mold grows in heavy furred carpets over floor and walls alike, and in places it has swallowed shapes that might once have been bodies. Dead flies lie in drifts along the foot of the wall. The hall runs east toward cleaner stone and west into a blackness that seems to wait.
rooms.22178: The walls of this narrow hall are pierced with hundreds of small holes, and from each one the point of an iron spike glints in whatever faint light you carry. The floor is studded with pressure plates disguised as worn flagstones. Somewhere within the stone, great counterweights shift with a grinding groan. The hall's only ways lead east and west, and every step between them is a gamble.
rooms.22159: Here the hall narrows until its walls almost brush your shoulders, and those walls are not still. With a slow, grinding patience they creep inward on hidden tracks, and the dust of their passage sifts down from the ceiling. The stones are stained dark at the height of a man's chest. The way east and the way west seem very far off in the blackness.
rooms.22161: The ceiling of this black hall is a single slab of iron hung on chains that run up into the dark, and it hangs lower than it should. Scraps of crushed armour are pressed flat into the floor beneath it like leaves in a book. A chain groans somewhere overhead. The hall leads east to the scorched passage and west toward a stretch that no one seems to have walked out of.
rooms.22104: Beyond the iron maiden the hall grows quiet again, though the dark here is total and the air is cold enough to ache in the teeth. Old blood has dried in a long smear along the floor, running from the east as if something was dragged this way. The walls bear the soot of torches that burned out long ago. The hall carries on west toward a grey glimmer of light.
rooms.14124: Grey light leaks into this part of the hall through a high crack in the wall, enough to show the full ruin of the place. Fallen ceiling stones lie where they dropped, and among them the rusted rim of a war-wagon wheel leans against the wall. Ash drifts in through the crack and settles over everything like fine grey flour. The hall runs east into the dark and west toward a bend in the wall.
rooms.14126: The hall runs straight along the inner wall here, its floor paved with slabs carved long ago with the sigils of the four horsemen: a crown, a sword, a scale and a skull. Most have been worn almost smooth by passing feet. A cold draught moves steadily from north to south as though the castle itself were breathing. The way runs north into shadow and south to a bend in the wall.
rooms.14128: Shattered weapon racks line this length of the hall, their pegs empty, their timbers split and blackened. A heap of broken arrow shafts lies in one corner, the fletching long since rotted to nothing. The air smells faintly of old oil and older blood. The hall runs on north and south between the racks.
rooms.14129: A crack runs the full height of the inner wall here, and through it seeps a faint red glow and a warmth that feels wrong in so cold a place. The stone around the crack is blistered and glassy. Ash lies in a fan across the floor beneath it. The hall continues north along the wall and south past a row of broken weapon racks.
rooms.14131: Chains are strung across this part of the hall at head height, hung with the dented helms of fallen knights like grim bells. When the draught stirs, they knock together with a hollow, tuneless sound. The floor beneath is gritty with flakes of rust. The hall leads north toward a bitter cold and south along the curve of the wall.
rooms.14133: A narrow stair is cut into the thickness of the wall here, climbing up toward the ragged walkway that runs along the castle's top. The hall turns at its foot, running east along the wall and south into a chill that bites through any cloak. The steps are worn to a dip in the middle, and a thin whine of wind comes down them from above. Bones lie wedged in the angle of the stair, as if someone fell there and was never moved.
rooms.14135: This stretch of hall is lined with tall niches, each holding the rusted shell of a suit of armour bolted upright to the stone. The helms are empty, but every visor has been turned to face the passage. The hall runs east along the wall and west toward a face of stone gouged by enormous claws. Dust lies thick and undisturbed in the niches.
rooms.14136: The hall here is hung with the war trophies of some ancient victory: shields nailed to the wall in rows, each one split clean through by a single blow. Beneath them a long stone table runs the length of the passage, bare but for a film of ash. The hall leads east toward the entrance chambers and west past a line of armoured niches. A faint cold wind sighs along the floor.
rooms.22002: The hall is black as pitch here, and the walls lean so close that they seem to listen. A low arch to the east opens onto the entrance chambers, the only break in the dark. Something has gouged long furrows into the floor, running west into the blackness where the hall carries on along the inner wall. The air is cold and tastes of rust.
rooms.14139: Four ways meet in this high, square chamber beneath a ceiling ribbed with blackened iron. A great brazier of bone and bronze stands cold in the centre, its bowl full of grey ash. The Inner Hall opens both to the north and to the south, while the inner corridor runs off east and west. The walls are hung with burned banners whose devices can no longer be read.
rooms.14140: The inner corridor is narrow and high, its walls rising into darkness where iron hooks dangle from the vault on lengths of chain. The floor is laid with black flags, polished smooth along a single worn track down the middle. To the west lies the junction of the inner halls, and to the east the corridor grows darker still. A low, steady draught carries the smell of cold ash.
rooms.22020: No light reaches this stretch of the inner corridor, and the dark seems to soak up sound as well. Underfoot, brittle things crunch with every step, too many and too small to be stones. The walls are cold and faintly greasy to the touch. The corridor runs on east and west, its ends invisible.
rooms.14142: The inner corridor widens here beside a heavy iron-banded doorway that opens north into a guard room. Spikes have been set into the door's frame point-outward, and old ash is trodden into the floor before it. To the east the corridor runs a short way further to its end, and to the west it stretches back into blackness. A rusted lantern hook juts from the wall, long empty.
rooms.22021: The inner corridor ends here against a wall of fused black stone, smooth as glass and warm to the touch, as if it had once run like wax. Nothing is carved on it and nothing breaks its face. The darkness is complete, and the silence is so deep that your own heartbeat sounds loud. The only way out lies back to the west.
rooms.14150: The Inner Hall is a long, lofty chamber whose roof is lost above a thicket of iron chains hung with the bones of men and beasts. Its floor is a mosaic of black and red stone, cracked and heaved but still showing the shape of a vast rider on a pale horse. A massive door of bone-white wood bound in iron stands to the south, and to the north the hall opens onto the junction of the inner halls. The air is cold enough to steam the breath.
rooms.14151: The guardian chambers begin here in a broad stone room ringed with empty pedestals, as though statues once stood watch and simply walked away. A door of black iron, graven with a skull, stands closed to the south. Archways lead east and west into further chambers, and the Inner Hall lies back to the north. Gouges in the floor around each pedestal show where great weight has shifted many times.
rooms.14154: This chamber is long and bare, its walls lined with deep alcoves that hold nothing but shadow and dust. The floor between them is scattered with shattered bone and the splintered remains of shields. Torch brackets of twisted iron jut from the walls, black with old soot. The chambers run on east, and west back toward the skull-graven door.
rooms.14155: A pair of colossal iron gauntlets is set into the wall here, palms open and fingers curled, each large enough to close around a man. Chains run from their wrists into the stone. The floor before them is cracked in a wide ring, as if something heavy has dropped there again and again. The chambers continue east and west through low, square doorways.
rooms.14156: The guardian chambers turn here, the passage bending in from the west and running on south into a deeper dark. Burned banners hang in a row along the wall, every one scorched into a ragged triangle. The stone floor is gritty with ash and fragments of bone, and the cold seems to come up through it. A single iron spike has been driven deep into the floor at the turn, its head worn bright by passing hands.
rooms.22022: This chamber lies in utter darkness, the walls rough and the ceiling so low it seems to press down on the crown of your head. A smell of mold and old iron hangs in the stale air. Bones crowd the corners, heaped as high as a man's waist. The way leads north toward the bannered turn of the chambers and south to the last of them.
rooms.14158: The guardian chambers end in a high, round room whose walls are carved floor to ceiling with armoured warriors kneeling in rows. Every kneeling figure has had its face chiselled away. In the centre of the floor a broad disc of iron is sunk flush with the stone, marked with a single handprint burned into the metal. The only way out leads back north into the dark.
rooms.14152: A narrow, steep-walled passage runs on from the skull-graven door toward the lair of Death, and every stone in it is cold as a grave. The walls are set with niches holding skulls, row upon row, their empty sockets turned toward the passage. A heavy door of blackened iron waits to the south, hot to the touch despite the chill. The guardian chambers lie back to the north.
rooms.14153: Two immense gates of black iron fill the end of this chamber, twice the height of any castle door and wrought with writhing figures that seem to move at the corner of the eye. A dull red glow beats behind them like a slow heart, and heat rolls from their seams in waves. The gates are sealed fast by chains as thick as a man's leg. The only way back is north, through the iron door into the entry-way.
rooms.14159: This chamber is bare stone from floor to ceiling, except for a long row of iron hooks along one wall where shields once hung. Their shapes still show as pale ovals on the soot-darkened stone. The air is colder here and very still. Archways lead east to the chamber of empty pedestals and west to further guardian chambers.
rooms.14160: The ceiling of this guardian chamber has partly fallen, and a slope of broken stone and bone fills one side of the room almost to the vault. A path has been cleared through the rubble, stamped hard by heavy feet. From somewhere above comes the faint, endless whisper of wind. The chambers continue east and west, the way west dim and choked with dust.

14207.description: Each pike is a shaft of black iron sunk into the rock, and each skull is fixed to its point with a twist of rusted wire. Some are human, some far larger, and all of them stare at the castle wall as though waiting for it to fall.

14105.description: The marks are grouped in fives, row after row, scratched with a knife point into the black stone. The last row ends in a single long gouge that runs off the edge of the tally and down the wall.

14126.keywords: sigils slabs crown sword scale skull
14126.description: Four sigils are carved in turn into the floor slabs: a crown for plague, a sword for war, a scale for hunger and a skull for the end of all things. Where feet have not worn them away, the grooves are still stained dark.

14150.description: The rider in the mosaic is drawn in black stone on a horse of pale bone-coloured tiles, a long blade held low at its side. Red tiles spread from the horse's hooves like spilled blood, and many of them have been prised up and carried off.

14158.description: The iron disc is as wide as a cartwheel and cold as the deep earth. The handprint burned into its centre is too long in the fingers to be a man's, and the metal around it is blistered as if from a great heat.

14153.description: The figures wrought into the gates are men and women caught in endless falling, their mouths open and their hands reaching up. Look too long and they seem to slip a little further down the iron.
